one_line_claim: For the same four-sample periodic Hann window, a coherent tone is calibrated by the sum of weights while white-noise power is calibrated by the sum of squared weights, yielding G_c=0.5 and ENBW=1.5 bins without conflating scalloping or the real-cosine factor of two.

design_contract.subject_role: Amber marks the coherent-tone path and every occurrence of its sum-of-weights quantity.
design_contract.contrast_role: Blue marks the independent-white-noise path and every occurrence of its squared-weight quantity.
design_contract.accept_role: Green marks only the correctly calibrated amplitude result.
reading_order: Read the shared N=4 Hann weights and their squares.
Split into the amber coherent-amplitude path and blue independent-noise-power path.
Follow numbered calculations to C_w correction and B_e.
Use the half-bin inset and real-cosine guard to prevent two common calibration substitutions.
Read the bottom synthesis as the invariant: sum w for tones, sum w squared for noise.
design_contract.graphics: Inline SVG is restricted to the paired weight bar rows and semantic split arrows; HTML provides layout and KaTeX provides all mathematical notation.
design_contract.responsive_layout: The two main panels use auto-fit minmax columns and wrap vertically when the standalone/page container narrows; result cards and the final synthesis also wrap.

numeric_audit: w=[0,0.5,1,0.5], sum w=2, normalized coherent gain G_c=2/4=0.5.
A matching unit complex tone gives X_w[1]=A C_w=2A; dividing by N gives 0.5A (-6.02 dB), while dividing by C_w gives A.
For finite N=4, |W(exp(j pi/N))|/|W(1)|=(2+sqrt(2))/4=0.8536, so positive scalloping loss is 1.38 dB.
For independent white noise, raw expected coefficient power is 1.5 sigma^2 and tone-calibrated power is 1.5 sigma^2/4=0.375 sigma^2.
ENBW is 4(1.5)/2^2=1.5 bins, 1.5 times the one-bin rectangular reference under the same tone calibration.
The real-cosine guard uses 2|X_w[k]|/C_w at interior positive bins and |X_w[k]|/C_w at DC or even-N Nyquist.

observed_defects: The real-cosine guard rendered the Markdown fragment $N$ literally because ordinary HTML text does not pass through MDX math processing.
fixes: Replaced the literal fragment with <M tex="N" size={12} /> so all mathematical notation uses KaTeX.

checks: No clipped title, panel border, formula, bar label, arrow, or bottom synthesis line.
No formula source rendered in red and no dollar-delimited text remained.
The shared input precedes the two paths and the numbered calculations read top to bottom.
Tone, noise, and calibrated roles are bound to amber, blue, and green in labels as well as borders/graphics.
Smallest labels remain legible at the rendered width.
Current-color text, axes, muted copy, and panel borders remain visible against the dark background.
Amber, blue, and green retain sufficient contrast and identical semantic roles.
Color-mix cards do not become opaque light patches or erase KaTeX text.
No clipping, collisions, broken TeX, misaligned arrowheads, or color-only status cues were found.
